text:
Alex: Heads-up — the onboarding sample app (bulk embeddings) started spiking 429s and we're seeing missing/invalid cursor behavior when retries/backpressure kick in. Anyone seen this pattern?

Marisol: Yup, I noticed it this morning. The sequence is weird: client hits quota -> server sends 429 with Retry-After sometimes, then the paginator sometimes fails to resume and we get a 410 on the next cursor. Feels like timing-sensitive cursor invalidation. :confused:

Samir: Saw similar during load test. The sample app does a naive concurrent fetch of pages which amplifies the burst. Code from sampleapp: 

```js
// buggy: fire all page fetches in parallel
const requests = []
for (const cursor of cursors) {
  requests.push(client.embeds.fetchPage({ cursor }))
}
await Promise.all(requests)
```

That means when a 429 arrives we end up with a bunch of concurrent retries and the next_page token can be stale by the time one of them succeeds.

Alex: Good catch. Also noticed the SDK doesn't consistently parse Retry-After values when they're floats or strings. Some responses had `Retry-After: 1.5` which the SDK treated as 1ms somehow (parsing bug).

Nina: I traced two issues: (1) our paginator implementation assumes strict sequential consumption of cursors; parallel consumers race. (2) auth refresh in SDK v0.5.2 can race with in-flight requests: if token refresh promise isn't deduped, multiple refreshes happen and a burst of requests is retried repeatedly. I opened a fix (PR linked).

Samir: Link?

Nina: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/489 — fixes retry-after parsing (accepts floats and quoted headers), adds a per-auth refresh mutex so refresh is deduped, and updates paginator to surface a concurrency warning when a user tries to iterate the same paginator from multiple loops.

Marisol: Thanks — for immediate mitigation we've added a client-side leaky-bucket limiter in the sample app and switched the embedding pagination to an async iterator consumed serially: 

```js
// safer: sequential iterate with backpressure
for await (const page of client.embeds.paginate({ query, pageSize: 200 })) {
  await processBatch(page.items)
}
```

Dave: Pushing a hotfix to sample-app now: set per-route concurrency to 3, add jittered backoff, and honor Retry-After precisely. Deploying to staging.

CI Bot: sample-app/staging deploy succeeded (build 2026-03-22_11:12) :white_check_mark:

Samir: After throttling down concurrency and deduping refresh, error rate dropped to baseline in our smoke run. Still seeing one edge where server returned `429` + no Retry-After header and SDK default backoff was too aggressive. Nina's PR adds a sensible default of 1s + jitter in that case.

Alex: Great. Action items: (1) merge Nina's PR and cut SDK patch release (0.5.3), (2) update sample-app to use per-route concurrency limiter and async-iterator pattern, (3) add a short doc in devex about "pagination + throttling pitfalls" with code examples.

Nina: I'll land the PR today and open the release. Also writing the doc; will ping for reviews.

Dave: I'll update the sample app PR to include a tiny helper `createLeakyBucket(limit, rate)` we can reuse.

Alex: Thanks all — this explains onboarding friction we've seen. Once SDK patch is out I'll re-run the onboarding smoke tests and update the crash report template. :thumbsup:
